newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Tranz Rail gets go-ahead on Clifford Bay.
newsitem.headline: Tranz Rail gets go-ahead on Clifford Bay.

text.p: Tranz Rail Ltd has been given the go ahead to build a ferry terminal at Clifford Bay, south of Blenheim, the New Zealand Press Association reported on Wednesday.
However, there is a raft of conditions accompanying the decision of which the first part alone runs to 200 pages.

Marlborough district councillors were notified of the special hearings committee's decision this morning although none of the major players, including applicant Tranz Rail, had been told of the decision by late morning.
Tranz Rail said it would not comment until it had had a chance to study the report.
If Tranz Rail does relocate, the implications would be enormous for the district, said Marborough Mayor Liz Davidson.
It will affect the riding and roading systems and the route through to Nelson.
Picton will need to refocus as a tourist destination, Davidson said.
Brian Fitzpatrick, managing director of Port Marlborough Ltd, which objected to the move south, had not seen the decision and would not comment until he had done so.
Jeff Pascoe, a Picton member of the district council, said the decision was no great surprise.

"We will have to look at the consent conditions and get a feel for the thing. If they are stringent enough Tranz Rail may even look at appealing it themselves. It may not even be viable for them to go " he said.
The decision was no great surprise to Dominion Salt Ltd, which put in a strong submission against the move to Clifford Bay, near the Lake Grassmere salt works.
"We will still be talking to Tranz Rail to see what we can do. We hope the salt works will be safeguarded by the conditions," said Dominion Salt general manager John Eggers.
